notes: A playtest senior in Bend, Oregon applied to a college in March, was admitted and enrolled the same day, and started college that afternoon while still in high school. Applications now wait for an answer and a place starts with the fall term after high school ends; both numbers are placeholders.
Whether a person is admitted at all is a separate open question (who-gets-into-college-and-what-it-costs); this one is only about timing.

A senior is not held to the degree path's minimum age of 18: finishing high school is treated as the entry rule for a degree, so a seventeen-year-old senior can apply. That is a design choice, not a sourced rule.
question: When a person applies to a US college for an associate's, bachelor's or master's degree, how long after applying do they usually hear back (regular decision, early decision or action, rolling admission, open-admission community colleges)? On what dates do fall, spring and other terms (winter, summer, quarter-system terms) usually begin? Is starting in the middle of the academic year, in January or at a quarter start, common for a new student, and does that differ between community colleges, public four-year colleges and graduate programs?

sourcesChecked.source: The shipped college directory (NCES IPEDS) as the game loads it
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Names colleges, their award levels and whether they report open admission. Says nothing about when applications are answered or when terms start.

sourcesChecked.source: The game's own K-12 calendar in src/simulation/school-stages.ts
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Gives when a child's high school ends (a placeholder between May 20 and June 15), which is when a senior's college place may begin. Says nothing about the college's own calendar.

title: When colleges answer applications and when their terms begin
usableAnswer: For each of community college, public four-year and graduate admission: a typical wait, or range, between applying and the decision, and whether it depends on when in the year the application is sent. For semester and quarter calendars: the usual start date, or window, of each term. A yes or no, by college type, on whether a new student may begin at a spring or other mid-year term.
whyItMatters: Every college now answers an application 45 days after it is sent (src/education/study-provider.ts:154, ADMISSION_DECISION_DAYS at line 157), and every new student starts on August 25, with no spring or quarter start (src/education/study-provider.ts:162, COLLEGE_FALL_TERM_START at line 166). A grown applicant who misses the fall waits most of a year, which may be wrong for community colleges and rolling admission.
